blocker_detail.what_failed: The dry_validate() schema check at SEALED status (in runner/run_pilot.py, around line 471) treats an empty-string endpoint value as 'not sealed' and adds an error to the dry-run result. The check uses `if v in (None, '', '<TO_BE_SEALED>')` which lumps a legitimately empty captured value together with 'unset' placeholders.
blocker_detail.why_endpoint_is_legitimately_empty: The endpoint capture rule (defined in runner/run_pilot.py, _capture_endpoint) tries `hermes -p <profile> config get --json <key>` for each key in ENDPOINT_KEYS_IN_PRIORITY_ORDER = ('model.base_url', 'model.endpoint_url', 'endpoint', 'api.base_url'). For both coa-e2-coa-s1 and coa-e2-control-s1, all four keys return 'Config key not set: <key>' (verified by direct CLI invocation). Per the documented capture rule, the captured endpoint value is therefore '' (empty string), which is a legitimate, deterministic, reproducible capture.
blocker_detail.why_modifying_the_frozen_runner_would_be: The PI authorization explicitly forbids modifying any of the 33 frozen candidate artifacts. runner/run_pilot.py is one of the 33. The schema check is part of the frozen contract.
blocker_detail.relationship_to_the_v0.4.2_technical_deb: The FREEZE-RECORD-v0.4.2.json recorded a non-blocking technical-debt note about REQUIRED_EXPECTED_KEYS in dry_validate() being non-load-bearing for execution safety. That note described the missing-fields check (six keys vs nine keys). It did not describe the empty-string rejection. The empty-string rejection is a separate issue that emerged when the SEALED manifest was first exercised with a legitimately empty endpoint.
blocker_detail.what_would_be_required_to_unblock: A narrowly scoped patch to the dry_validate() schema check in runner/run_pilot.py to treat a legitimately captured empty endpoint (or any other legitimately captured empty value) as sealed. This would require either: (a) a new v0.4.3 candidate with the schema check loosened to `if v is None or v == '<TO_BE_SEALED>'`; or (b) a PI ruling that the empty-string rejection is itself a freeze-blocking defect and the schema check should be relaxed without a new candidate. Either path requires explicit PI authorization because it modifies the frozen runner contract.
